answer: Only one bonded tram-brakeman may claim the numbered basalt siding under the east ridge. She posts 36.2 POA, must pin her named brass tag inside the hollow of the brake column before the 19:05 shift bell, and after each loaded descent she records the tram's stamped tare on a carbon slip the yard clerk can match to the scale tape. If a gale warning is flying she must also log a 30-second anemometer reading on the same slip. A second tag, a missing slip, or a tare that disagrees by more than 0.8 kg forfeits 18.1 POA and voids the siding; a repeat mismatch bars her from the next two shifts.
